segments: The charity shop near the bus station.
The manager, Denise, and another volunteer called Paul.
I've got a story from my own week.
I tried to sort out a cupboard at home and found three different chargers that didn't fit anything I own.
What did you do on your first day?
They showed me the till and how to tag the clothes.
I had to put the hangers the same way round.
What happened when a customer came in?
A woman asked if we had any blue coats.
I looked through the rail but I couldn't find one.
She said to check the back room.
There were some blue jumpers but no coats.
How did you feel when you couldn't find it?
I was worried I'd done it wrong.
You were worried because you hadn't found the coat.
I didn't know if I was allowed to go in the back room without asking.
Denise showed me where the stock was kept and then I put the jumpers out.
Did anything else happen during the shift?
A man brought in a bag of books.
I put them on the donations shelf.
What happened at the end of the shift?
Paul showed me how to lock the back door.
So you started volunteering at the charity shop, learnt the till and clothing tags, asked Denise about the blue coat, helped with the jumpers and put donated books on the shelf.
Paul showed you how to lock the back door before you went home.

written.summary: The child told about volunteering at the charity shop near the bus station. The child met the manager Denise and another volunteer called Paul. The child learned to tag clothes, use the till, and organize the stock. The child helped a woman find blue coats but couldn't find any. The child asked Denise about going into the back room and then put the jumpers out. The child also put books on the donations shelf and then went home.
